Shyanne-Lee Tatnell was reported missing from a Launceston youth hostel in 2023. Her remains were found three months later. (Supplied: Michelle Hubbard)

The trial of Christopher Mark Jordan, 39, who is accused of murdering 14-year-old Shyanne-Lee Tatnell, has been set for April 2027.

The Burnie teenager's remains were found about three months after she went missing.

The trial is expected to run for five weeks.

A man accused of murdering a Tasmanian teenager will face trial in April next year, almost four years after her death.

Scottsdale man Christopher Mark Jordan, who has pleaded not guilty to murdering 14-year-old Shyanne-Lee Tatnell, appeared in the Supreme Court in Launceston via video link from Risdon Prison today.

Justice Michael Brett told the court the trial date has been listed for April 19 next year, four years after the Burnie teenager went missing while staying at a Launceston youth hostel.

Following an extensive search, her remains were found almost three months later, off a dirt track at Nabowla, north-east of Launceston.

Mr Jordan was arrested the next day.

He was charged with murder and pleaded not guilty in 2024.

The trial is expected to take five weeks and will be heard by Justice Brett.

Another directions hearing, in which parties are expected to discuss any pre-trial issues, has been listed for November 27, 2026.
